title: SDK connection models: language shim gaps, token patterns & resumable-stream ergonomics
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background:
Several enterprise customers (Acme Finance, Orion Health, and a stealth SPaaS customer) have submitted non-bug requests asking for: 1) idiomatic client bindings in Go and Java that mirror our Python/TS ergonomics, 2) clearer token rotation patterns for long-running sessions, and 3) resumable/restoreable streaming semantics for flaky mobile/edge networks. These requests reveal two correlated risks for adoption: language gaps (clients can't adopt if a common language is missing) and engineering/UX mismatches in session/auth patterns that increase support burden and security risk.

Goal:
Triage incoming SDK/client requests and produce a prioritization decision and a minimal actionable plan that the engineering team can scope. Deliverables: a triage rubric, prioritized list of language/adaptor work, one spike PR for a resumable-stream prototype, and a short RFC capturing our recommended token/session patterns for enterprise usage.

Triage rubric (proposed scoring, 0-5 each):
- Customer criticality (size/contract risk)
- Frequency across intake (how many customers asked)
- Engineering complexity (estimated dev + infra)
- Security/regulatory constraints (KMS/HSM integrations, audit needs)
- UX delta vs existing SDKs (how far from parity)
Total score determines priority band: 18-25 = P0 immediate; 12-17 = P1 planned; 6-11 = P2 backlog; <=5 = P3 research.

Initial observations (from intake analysis):
- Languages requested most: Go (18 unique asks), Java (12), C# (6), Ruby (4), Kotlin (3). Python/TS remain dominant in usage but are already well-covered.
- Auth patterns: token rotation for long-lived connections and clear guidance for service account vs end-user session tokens were repeated in enterprise tickets.
- Streaming ergonomics: customers want resumable streams (client can reattach and continue from last acknowledged token/offset), client-side buffering guidance, and sample code for exponential backoff and idempotency on partial completions.

Proposed immediate decisions (In Review):
1) Quick wins (target for Q1): deliver first-class Go adapter that reuses the existing JS/Python ergonomics surface (builder pattern, typed streaming callbacks). Score justification: high customer_count + moderate engineering effort.
2) Auth patterns RFC (target: 2-week authoring): produce a security-reviewed RFC that defines: recommended token lifetimes, refresh rotation patterns for streaming sessions, guidance for delegated service accounts, and examples for rotating credentials in Dedicated/Private deployments.
3) Resumable-stream spike (1 sprint): eng spike to prototype resumable-stream semantics with server-side offsets and client-side persistence. Deliver a reference implementation in TypeScript and Go + a small e2e test harness.
4) Backlog languages: C#/Ruby/Kotlin to be scheduled after Go/Java parity. Provide community-maintained adapters guidance in the interim.

Acceptance criteria:
- Approved RFC that includes security sign-off and KMS/HSM integration notes.
- PR merged with a minimal Go adapter example (README, quickstart, and streaming sample).
- Prototype resumable-stream PoC with runbook and benchmark notes demonstrating reconnect < 2s median restore for normal network blips.
- Documentation pages and code samples published under /docs/sdk/compatibility and release notes in sdk-2026.01.

Links & artifacts:
- Intake spreadsheet (internal drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/enterprise-sdk-intake-2025Q4
- Draft RFC (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Streaming+Resumption+RFC
- Spike PR (ts prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/7342
- Design notes for Go adapter ergonomics: https://drive.redwood.ai/file/d/1GoAdapterDesign/view

Open questions: 
- Do we need a formal deprecation policy for community adapters we will not own? (PM decision)
- Is the resumable-stream semantics compatible with existing KV cache and batching strategies in the runtime? (Eng dependency ENG-40220)
- Should we include first-class support for platform-managed token rotation (on Redwood-hosted tokens) or leave rotation to customer-managed refresh flows? (Security decision required)

Next steps / owner assignments:
- PM (Sofia) to finalize rubric and circulate to Eng/Design/Security by 2025-11-07.
- Eng (Liam) to scope the Go adapter spike and open initial PR by 2025-11-14.
- Security (Rashid Khan) to schedule a 45-min review of RFC draft by 2025-11-18.
- Docs (Aisha Patel) to reserve doc pages and draft quickstart templates after spike completes.

Notes from cross-functional sync (2025-11-10):
- Design prefers a unified builder pattern across languages to minimize cognitive switching; proposal: fluent builder + optional callback vs async iterator depending on language norms.
- Eng raised concern about maintaining parity across SDKs; suggested introducing a compatibility test harness that runs core examples across languages on CI. Action: ENG-40220 to scope harness.
